title: Unidirectional Monitors (erlang:monitor/2, spawn_monitor/1), 'DOWN' Messages & The noproc Invariant
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates unidirectional process monitors, crash isolation, timeout worker termination, and the noproc dead-PID invariant.

otpDocCards.description: Atomically creates a new process and starts a monitor to watch it.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) allocation with atomic monitor setup.

otpDocCards.description: Starts monitoring target. If target is dead, sends noproc DOWN message.
Removes monitor and flushes any pending DOWN message from mailbox.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) deletion plus scan of mailbox.

mentalModelCheck.question: What message does the BEAM deliver if you call `erlang:monitor(process, DeadPid)` on a process that already terminated?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
DeadPid = spawn(fun() -> ok end),
timer:sleep(50),
MRef = erlang:monitor(process, DeadPid).

options.label: The runtime places `{'DOWN', MRef, process, DeadPid, noproc}` into the caller’s mailbox immediately, avoiding any check-then-act race conditions.
options.explanation: Correct! The BEAM guarantees that monitoring a non-existent process immediately delivers `{'DOWN', MRef, process, DeadPid, noproc}`, completely preventing check-then-monitor race conditions.

options.label: erlang:monitor/2 crashes with badarg.
options.explanation: erlang:monitor/2 does not crash on dead PIDs; it sends a noproc DOWN message.

options.label: The caller hangs waiting for an exit signal.
options.explanation: Monitors do not wait or block callers.
